title: HfO2/Al2O3/SiO2 three-material custom stack
scientific_hypothesis: A three-material system (HfO2/Al2O3/SiO2) enables better index matching and reduced stress compared to two-material systems, improving both UV transmission and blocking within 30 layers.
design_principle: Three materials provide additional degrees of freedom for impedance matching at interfaces, reducing reflection losses in the passband while maintaining blocking performance. Al2O3 serves as an intermediate index layer between HfO2 and SiO2.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | Al2O3 | SiO2 | HfO2 | Al2O3 | SiO2 | HfO2_cavity | SiO2 | Al2O3 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Al2O3 | HfO2 | SiO2_substrate
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 14 layers
Material sequence order (fixed for this route)
soft_objectives: Minimize interface reflection losses through index grading
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count is 14, well under 30-layer limit
Three materials require three deposition sources or sequential processing
All materials are conventional e-beam depositable
theory_basis: Impedance matching theory for multilayer stacks
expected_advantages: Reduced interface reflections through index grading
Better stress distribution across the stack
known_risks: Risk of material interdiffusion at interfaces
Optimization complexity increases with material count
execution_request_english: Design a custom three-material bandpass filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack: 14 layers alternating HfO2, Al2O3, SiO2 (Gao) with one HfO2 cavity layer at position 8. Total 14 layers. Optimize all individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm while minimizing transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Materials: hfo2, al2o3, SiO2 (Gao).
